# Dovetail — Style Reference

> Bitmap type spliced into a darkroom contact sheet. Inter 600 headlines on #0a0a0a near-black, a pixel serif breaking in mid-sentence, 1px hairlines at eight percent white, and one cobalt key held in reserve.

**Theme:** dark

Values are measured from the live site and normalized; names, roles and recommendations are interpretation. Font lists are independent, not paired by position. Example prompts describe reconstructions, not the site's source code.

Dovetail speaks a darkroom-terminal product language. A near-black canvas of #0a0a0a carries every section, and the surface stack climbs only through #191919 panels, #fafafa14 frosted glass and a single #ffffff inverted button. The chromatic budget is two hues. Signal Cobalt #0044ff covers filled actions, one testimonial slab and a lone data glyph. Amethyst Twin #a65cff is reserved for the Digital Twins product. Every other saturated pixel lives inside product mockups or cut-out photographs. Typography carries the thesis. Inter 600 runs headlines at 160px and 96px, tracked to -2.3px and -2px. Mid-sentence, a word breaks into PP Mondwest, a bitmap serif set at 120px so its smaller x-height lands on Inter's line. JetBrains Mono at 12px uppercase with 1px tracking labels everything machine-side. Hierarchy comes from a 1.67 jump between 96px and 160px and from white opacity steps, not from color. Shape is one 8px radius, and elevation is 1px #ffffff14 hairlines. The site reads as a research lab's terminal printout rather than a SaaS dashboard.

## Tokens — Colors

| Name | Value | Token | Role |
|---|---|---|---|
| Onyx Canvas | `#0a0a0a` | `--color-onyx-canvas` | Body, footer and section backgrounds, plus the Paper button's label (27 background uses). It is a warm-neutral near-black, so it reads as printed ink rather than the cold void of #000000. |
| Carbon Scrim | `#0a0a0aa3` | `--color-carbon-scrim` | Overlay veil behind the open mega menu and translucent layers over the matrix texture (12 uses). It dims the page to 64% without hiding it. Do not use it as a card fill. |
| Graphite Panel | `#191919` | `--color-graphite-panel` | Stat card, mega-menu panel and announcement strip. It is the single opaque step above canvas, so depth comes from tone rather than shadow. |
| Frosted Glass | `#fafafa14` | `--color-frosted-glass` | Process chips such as INDEXATION and SYNTHESIS, code-action chips and hover fills (10 uses). Paired with a 12px backdrop blur, it lets the glyph rain show through. |
| Paper | `#ffffff` | `--color-paper` | Fill of the nav "Book a demo" button and pure-white label text (136 text uses). It is the inverted surface. Do not use it for full-width sections, because it breaks the darkroom. |
| Fog Ink | `#fafafa` | `--color-fog-ink` | Headlines, active tab text, chip labels and quote text (138 uses, the most frequent text color). It is a half-step off white, which softens halation on near-black. |
| Mist Caption | `#ffffffa3` | `--color-mist-caption` | Inactive accordion tabs, menu descriptions and attribution lines (62 uses). Hierarchy by 64% opacity is the system's substitute for gray swatches. |
| Ash Caption | `#a7a7a7` | `--color-ash-caption` | Footnotes, stat captions, announcement text and monochrome logo tint (14 uses). This is the quietest legible text. Do not drop body copy below it. |
| Quartz Hairline | `#ffffff14` | `--color-quartz-hairline` | Card outlines, panel borders, mockup frames and nav hover fills (21 border uses). It is the workhorse edge that replaces shadow everywhere. |
| Frosted Border | `#fafafa29` | `--color-frosted-border` | The 1px ring on glass process chips (10 uses). It doubles the hairline's opacity so translucent chips keep a readable edge over texture. |
| Steel Border | `#ffffff3d` | `--color-steel-border` | Ghost button outline and the active accordion divider (11 uses). It is the strongest neutral line, reserved for interactive edges. |
| Signal Cobalt | `#0044ff` | `--color-signal-cobalt` | Primary CTA fill, the testimonial slab and the pixel arrow on the 30hrs stat (7 fills, 5 text uses). It is the only actionable hue. Do not tint backgrounds or body links with it. |
| Amethyst Twin | `#a65cff` | `--color-amethyst-twin` | Digital Twins widget title, its outline ring and the twin icon. It is a product-scoped accent. Do not promote it to the primary CTA color or to general highlights. |

## Tokens — Typography

### Inter — the human voice: dense, semibold, negatively tracked headlines and medium-weight body · `--font-inter`

- **Substitute:** Inter itself is free (Google Fonts, variable): use it at the same 400/500/600/700. Geist at 600 for display matches the stroke closely. Manrope at 600 draws slightly wider and lighter, so add -0.5px of extra tracking at 96px and above.
- **Weights:** 400, 500, 600, 700
- **Sizes:** 12px, 14px, 16px, 18px, 20px, 24px, 32px, 40px, 96px, 160px, 170px
- **Line height:** 0.875 (160px), 1.0 (170px), 1.042 (96px), 1.05 (40px), 1.25 (32px), 1.333 (24px), 1.4 (20px), 1.5 (16px), 1.571 (14px)
- **Letter spacing:** -4px at 170px, -2.3px at 160px, -2px at 96px, -1.2px at 40px, -1px at 32px and at the 24px weight-700 numbered titles, -0.5px at 24px emphasis, -0.25px at 20px and 24px, 0 at 16px and below
- **OpenType features:** `"liga"`
- **Role:** Weight 600 at display sizes is deliberate: the headlines are loud blocks of ink, not the hushed 400 weight many AI-era sites wear. The body workhorse is 500 at 16px (93 uses) rather than the conventional 400, which keeps small text sturdy on near-black. The ratio from 96px to 160px is 1.67, far beyond a Perfect Fourth (1.333). The scale is two-tier: a compact Major Third (1.25) body ladder from 16px to 20px to 24px, then a cliff into poster type. Tracking tightens in proportion to size, so every headline sets as a solid slab ready to be punctured.

### JetBrains Mono — the machine's labelling voice: uppercase, tracked, small · `--font-jetbrains-mono`

- **Substitute:** JetBrains Mono is free: use it at 400. IBM Plex Mono at 400 draws marginally heavier, which is acceptable. Geist Mono at 400 matches the stroke.
- **Weights:** 400
- **Sizes:** 12px, 14px
- **Line height:** 1.0 (12px), 1.4 (14px), 1.43 (14px chips)
- **Letter spacing:** 1px at 12px, 1px at 14px
- **OpenType features:** `"liga"`
- **Role:** Every instance is uppercase at 1px tracking (53 uses). That makes the mono a labelling register, used for column eyebrows, process chips and corner tags, and keeps it out of reading text. The 1.0 line height on 12px labels is intentionally tight, so labels sit like stamped serial numbers. The pairing tells the visitor which words were written by people (Inter) and which are system output (mono).

### PP Mondwest — the pixel interruption: a bitmap serif spliced into Inter sentences · `--font-pp-mondwest`

- **Substitute:** VT323 at 400 is thinner, so set it 5% larger than the original size. Pixelify Sans at 400 matches the stair-stepped stroke weight but loses the serifs. Prefer VT323 when the serif silhouette matters.
- **Weights:** 400
- **Sizes:** 24px, 96px, 120px
- **Line height:** 0.833 (120px), 1.0 (96px), 1.0 (24px)
- **Letter spacing:** -2px at 120px, 0 at 96px, -1px at 24px
- **OpenType features:** `"liga"`
- **Role:** Mondwest appears only 13 times, and that scarcity is the point. It replaces one or two words inside a 96px Inter headline ("customer", "rich context") and renders the 30hrs stat. It is set at 120px inside a 96px line because its x-height runs smaller than Inter's, and the 1.25× boost restores optical parity. Where convention pairs a serif display with a sans body, Dovetail pairs two display voices inside the same sentence.

### Type Scale

| Role | Family | Weight | Size | Line Height | Letter Spacing | Token |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| small | JetBrains Mono | 400 | 12px | 1.0 | 1px | `--text-small` |
| caption | Inter | 500 | 12px | 1.333 | 0px | `--text-caption` |
| body-sm | Inter | 400 | 14px | 1.571 | 0px | `--text-body-sm` |
| body | Inter | 500 | 16px | 1.5 | 0px | `--text-body` |
| body-lg | Inter | 400 | 20px | 1.4 | -0.25px | `--text-body-lg` |
| subheading | Inter | 500 | 24px | 1.333 | -0.25px | `--text-subheading` |
| heading-sm | Inter | 600 | 32px | 1.25 | -1px | `--text-heading-sm` |
| heading | Inter | 600 | 40px | 1.05 | -1.2px | `--text-heading` |
| heading-lg | Inter | 600 | 96px | 1.042 | -2px | `--text-heading-lg` |
| display | Inter | 600 | 160px | 0.875 | -2.3px | `--text-display` |

## Do's and Don'ts

### Do

- Set every headline in Inter 600 with size-proportional negative tracking (-2px at 96px, -2.3px at 160px) — the tight slab is what the pixel word punctures.
- Splice exactly one phrase per headline into PP Mondwest 400 at 1.25× the Inter size (120px inside a 96px line) — the boost compensates for Mondwest's smaller x-height so both faces share a cap line.
- Build depth from #0a0a0a canvas to #191919 panel to #fafafa14 glass with 1px #ffffff14 hairlines — tonal layering is the elevation system.
- Label system output in JetBrains Mono 12px uppercase at 1px tracking — the mono register signals machine-generated content, and Inter signals human voice.
- Use 8px radius on buttons, cards, chips and nav items, and 4px on images and inner tiles — two radii keep the geometry engineered rather than playful.
- Step text hierarchy through opacity: #fafafa for primary, #ffffffa3 for secondary, #a7a7a7 for tertiary — the canvas stays monochrome and hierarchy remains legible.
- Hold sections 160px apart inside a 1512px container with 124px gutters — the generous rhythm gives 96px headlines room to read as posters.

### Don't

- Don't set a full headline in PP Mondwest — the thesis is an interruption mid-sentence, and a full pixel line reads as a novelty font rather than the machine cutting into human speech.
- Don't make #0044ff a link color, icon tint or section background beyond the single testimonial slab — once cobalt decorates, the 40px CTA stops being the only thing to press.
- Don't add drop shadows to cards or panels — the one `0px 2px 4px` shadow belongs to the Paper nav button, and a shadowed #191919 card on #0a0a0a muddies the hairline system.
- Don't reach for 9999px pill buttons, the conventional SaaS shape — the 8px corner is shared by chips, menus and cards, and a pill would orphan the CTA.
- Don't use #a65cff for generic highlights, badges or gradients — it is scoped to Digital Twins, and borrowing it dissolves the product's identity.
- Don't loosen display leading to the conventional 1.1–1.2 — 160px sits at 0.875 (140px), and looser lines let the inline photo objects float apart from the words.
- Don't set body copy in pure #ffffff at weight 400 across long passages — the measured default is #fafafa at 500 on 16px, and the half-step off white prevents halation on #0a0a0a. This is non-negotiable for reading text.

## Agent Prompt Guide

**Quick Color Reference**
- canvas: #0a0a0a (Onyx Canvas)
- card surface: #191919 (Graphite Panel)
- primary text: #fafafa (Fog Ink)
- secondary text: #ffffffa3 (Mist Caption)
- hairline: #ffffff14 (Quartz Hairline)
- product accent: #a65cff (Amethyst Twin)
- primary action: #0044ff (filled action)

**Color in Data**
Charts and heat maps use #0044ff only as solid 4px-radius cells or bars at full and 40% opacity on #191919, with all remaining cells in #ffffff14, so cobalt marks the signal and the grid stays neutral.

**Example Component Prompts**

1. Build a Primary Action Button: a `<button>` with background #0044ff, text #fafafa, no border, border-radius 8px, padding 10px 16px, height 40px. Set the label in Inter at 14px, weight 600, line-height 18px, letter-spacing 0, with no shadow. Place it 16px left of a ghost button with transparent background, 1px solid #ffffff3d border, the same 8px radius, padding, size and type, and text #fafafa. Both sit on #0a0a0a.

2. Build a hero section: background #0a0a0a, inner container max-width 1512px with 124px horizontal padding. Add a centered h1 "Feed the facts machine" in Inter 600 at 160px, line-height 140px, letter-spacing -2.3px, color #fafafa, across two lines. After "Feed", insert an inline cut-out PNG of a photocopier 140px tall with no border, radius or shadow, aligned to the baseline. Add 64px below, then a row of ten monochrome customer logos tinted #a7a7a7, evenly distributed across 1264px. Add 64px below that, then a product mockup frame 1264px wide on #0a0a0a with a 1px solid #ffffff14 border and 8px radius.

3. Build a section headline with a pixel splice: an h2 in Inter 600 at 96px, line-height 100px, letter-spacing -2px, color #fafafa, reading "Build your customer context layer". Wrap only "customer" in a span set in PP Mondwest (fallback VT323) at weight 400, 120px, line-height 100px, letter-spacing -2px, same color. Below it, 48px down, add a 20px Inter 400 paragraph, line-height 28px, letter-spacing -0.25px, color #ffffffa3, max-width 568px. Follow with the cobalt and ghost button pair 32px beneath.

4. Build a stat card: background #191919, 1px solid #ffffff14 border, border-radius 8px, padding 48px, no shadow. Top: a stair-stepped up-arrow glyph in #0044ff, then "30hrs" in PP Mondwest 400 at 96px, line-height 96px, color #fafafa. Bottom, 64px lower: the label "Weekly time saved per user" in Inter 600 at 16px, line-height 24px, color #fafafa. Beneath it, 4px below: a caption in Inter 400 at 14px, line-height 22px, color #a7a7a7.

5. Build a navigation bar: height 88px, transparent over #0a0a0a, position relative (not sticky), inside a 1512px container with 124px padding. Left: an 18×20px logomark in #ffffff, then six triggers (Product, Solutions, Resources, Enterprise, Customers, Pricing) in Inter 600 at 14px, color #ffffff, padding 10px 16px, radius 8px, hover background #ffffff14. Right: a "Log in" text button with the same type, then a button with background #ffffff, text #0a0a0a, radius 8px, padding 10px 16px. Give that button the shadow `rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.45) 0px 2px 4px 0px, rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.8) 0px 0px 0px 1px inset`.

## Do's and Don'ts

### Do

- Set every headline in Inter 600 with size-proportional negative tracking (-2px at 96px, -2.3px at 160px) — the tight slab is what the pixel word punctures.
- Splice exactly one phrase per headline into PP Mondwest 400 at 1.25× the Inter size (120px inside a 96px line) — the boost compensates for Mondwest's smaller x-height so both faces share a cap line.
- Build depth from #0a0a0a canvas to #191919 panel to #fafafa14 glass with 1px #ffffff14 hairlines — tonal layering is the elevation system.
- Label system output in JetBrains Mono 12px uppercase at 1px tracking — the mono register signals machine-generated content, and Inter signals human voice.
- Use 8px radius on buttons, cards, chips and nav items, and 4px on images and inner tiles — two radii keep the geometry engineered rather than playful.
- Step text hierarchy through opacity: #fafafa for primary, #ffffffa3 for secondary, #a7a7a7 for tertiary — the canvas stays monochrome and hierarchy remains legible.
- Hold sections 160px apart inside a 1512px container with 124px gutters — the generous rhythm gives 96px headlines room to read as posters.

### Don't

- Don't set a full headline in PP Mondwest — the thesis is an interruption mid-sentence, and a full pixel line reads as a novelty font rather than the machine cutting into human speech.
- Don't make #0044ff a link color, icon tint or section background beyond the single testimonial slab — once cobalt decorates, the 40px CTA stops being the only thing to press.
- Don't add drop shadows to cards or panels — the one `0px 2px 4px` shadow belongs to the Paper nav button, and a shadowed #191919 card on #0a0a0a muddies the hairline system.
- Don't reach for 9999px pill buttons, the conventional SaaS shape — the 8px corner is shared by chips, menus and cards, and a pill would orphan the CTA.
- Don't use #a65cff for generic highlights, badges or gradients — it is scoped to Digital Twins, and borrowing it dissolves the product's identity.
- Don't loosen display leading to the conventional 1.1–1.2 — 160px sits at 0.875 (140px), and looser lines let the inline photo objects float apart from the words.
- Don't set body copy in pure #ffffff at weight 400 across long passages — the measured default is #fafafa at 500 on 16px, and the half-step off white prevents halation on #0a0a0a. This is non-negotiable for reading text.

## Elevation

- **Paper nav button (the only shadowed element, 2 uses):** `rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.45) 0px 2px 4px 0px, rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.8) 0px 0px 0px 1px inset` — a 2px drop plus a bright inset ring makes the button read as a physical key lit from above.
- **Cards, panels, mega menu and mockup frames:** `none` — depth is the tonal step from #0a0a0a to #191919 plus a 1px #ffffff14 hairline, unlike the conventional layered card shadows of light-mode SaaS.
- **Glass process chips:** `none` — elevation is simulated by backdrop-filter blur(12px) and a 1px #fafafa29 ring, so the chip floats by refraction rather than by cast shadow.

## Imagery

Imagery comes in three registers, none of them stock photography of people at desks. The first is cut-out photographs of analogue office objects placed inline inside headlines at cap height: a photocopier wearing googly eyes, a magnifier over a fingerprint, an overstuffed manila folder. They are unframed, carry no radius and no shadow, and sit flush against the type. The second is product screenshots rebuilt as dark UI mockups in 8px hairline frames on #0a0a0a, with 4px inner tiles. The third is decorative pixel art: a falling glyph-rain texture behind sections, a violet pixel ghost for Digital Twins, and a soft violet glow under the chat widget. All of these are decorative and none is a system token. Icons are 16px single-weight line glyphs. The narrative is old office paperwork fed into a pixel machine that returns structured context.

## Layout

Content sits in a 1512px container with 124px gutters, which yields a 1264px working width. Sections are separated by 160px and pace themselves as posters. The hero is a centered, two-line 160px Inter headline, "Feed the facts machine", with a photo object inline. Under it run a 10-across monochrome logo row and a full-width product mockup. Each later section repeats one pattern: a 96px spliced headline left-aligned or centered, then a 20px body paragraph with paired buttons. Below that comes a two-column split of a 510px accordion against media, or a 614px + 614px image pair. Proof arrives as a 2-column row: a wide cobalt slab and a narrower graphite stat card. There is no pricing grid on the home page. The nav is 88px, transparent and not sticky, with the logomark and six triggers left and Log in and Paper button right. The footer is a 769px block on #0a0a0a with mono-eyebrowed link columns and a 170px Inter wordmark. At 375px, set headlines at 40px and section gaps at 64px. Overall density: spacious.

## Pixel Splice Discipline

The defining move is a headline that switches typefaces mid-sentence: Inter 600 for the human claim, PP Mondwest for the word the machine renders. The discipline is quantity and calibration. Use one Mondwest phrase per headline (13 total uses across a 10-section page), set at 1.25× the surrounding Inter size so 120px Mondwest matches 96px Inter optically. What breaks it is a Mondwest headline, a Mondwest button, Mondwest body text, or a splice set at the same nominal size, which makes the pixel word shrink and look like a rendering bug. To extend the system, splice only nouns that name data or context ("customer", "rich context"). Reuse Mondwest for one numeric stat per section, and pair any new splice with at most one inline photo object.

## Cobalt Rationing

The chromatic budget is two hues, and cobalt does all the commercial work. #0044ff fills the primary button, floods exactly one testimonial slab and colors one pixel arrow. Everything else on a 548,927px-tall page is achromatic. That rationing makes a 40px button outrank a 160px headline. It would break if cobalt became link text, an icon tint, a gradient, a section background or a second filled button in the same viewport. Amethyst #a65cff is fenced the same way, around Digital Twins only. To extend the system, give any new product its own scoped accent the way Twins owns violet, keep it inside that product's widget, and leave filled actions exclusively cobalt.

## Opacity Hierarchy

Instead of the conventional gray ramp (gray-300 to gray-700), Dovetail ranks content by how much white survives. #fafafa carries headlines, #ffffffa3 carries secondary copy and inactive tabs, and #a7a7a7 carries footnotes. Lines follow the same logic: #ffffff14 for passive edges, #fafafa29 for glass chips and #ffffff3d for interactive outlines. Introducing tinted grays (bluish slate, warm taupe) would break it, because they would read as a third hue. So would adding mid-level opacities such as 50% or 80% that blur the three clear steps. To extend the system, map any new state onto an existing rung. Disabled states take #a7a7a7, a new divider takes #ffffff14, and a focus ring takes #ffffff3d at 2px.

## Similar Brands

- **Dovetail** — shares Linear's near-black canvas, Inter-led type and 1px translucent hairlines around full-width product mockups. Linear's headlines stay smaller and grayer, with no typeface splicing.
- **Dovetail** — shares Vercel's #0a0a0a-class canvas and uppercase monospace labels beside a grotesk. Vercel stays fully monochrome, without a saturated cobalt CTA.
- **Dovetail** — shares Warp's use of monospace as a brand register for machine output on dark surfaces. Dovetail confines mono to 12–14px labels instead of hero copy.
- **Dovetail** — shares Raycast's blurred glass chips and inverted white header button on dark. Raycast leans on glows and gradients where Dovetail uses tonal steps.
- **Dovetail** — competes with Maze in research tooling, and both sell research insight to product teams. Maze uses a light, illustrated canvas, while Dovetail uses a dark terminal with pixel type.
